name: package_arf1_flat_touch_v1
description: Full-package replay: vary ARF1 flat-resistance touch params within the server-reproduced crypto_income_static_v1 baseline. All ATT1, breakdown, MTPB params locked at baseline. Server baseline rerun on 2026-05-26 produced +73.96%, PF 1.591, DD 5.16%, 436 trades; only combos that beat that same-runtime benchmark qualify for promotion.

_notes.baseline: Server runtime crypto_income_static_v1 rerun 2026-05-26: +73.96%, PF 1.591, DD 5.16%, 436 trades, 2 negative months, streak 1 — promotion gate
_notes.blocker: ARF1 flat touch may be too selective: RES_TOUCH_BUFFER_ATR default and MIN_RSI=52 could be filtering valid resistance touches where price approaches but doesn't wick perfectly.
_notes.hypothesis: Widening touch buffer from 0.25→0.45 ATR catches looser approaches to flat resistance. Relaxing RSI floor 52→48 adds volume when resistance is strong regardless of momentum. REJECT_BELOW_RES_ATR tunes rejection wick sharpness.
_notes.interaction: RES_TOUCH_BUFFER_ATR (approach zone) and REJECT_BELOW_RES_ATR (rejection amplitude) have opposing effects on volume vs quality — sweep their interaction space explicitly.
_notes.promotion_gate: Exact baseline protocol and same server runtime: 365d ending 2026-04-25, risk_pct=1%, max_positions=5, fees/slippage=6/2 bps. Must beat net +73.96 and PF 1.591 with DD <= 5.17%, negative months <= 2, streak <= 1 before promotion.
_notes.run_after: att1_density_v3_more_pivots_v1 completes — can run in parallel with package_breakdown_rsi_v1 if server load allows
_notes.expected_time: Full-package annual runs are expensive; use bounded jobs and monitor resource load while running 48 combos.
